vendor: unpack vanna at 365d0617c1a4567ffee1b19b40c27feb4206bfcf

Upstream tree unpacked from the codeload archive (no .git in the archive).
git clone/ls-remote fail on this machine, so local commit hashes are not
upstream hashes. LICENSE kept byte-identical (MIT, Vanna.AI).

fix(sqlite): detect result sets from cursor.description, keep empty columns, commit RETURNING

run_sql classified statements by the first SQL token, so a leading comment,
WITH ... SELECT and VALUES fell into the write branch: rows were dropped and
rows_affected=-1 was returned.  A SELECT with no rows returned pd.DataFrame()
and lost the requested columns.  INSERT/UPDATE ... RETURNING crashed with
'cannot commit transaction - SQL statements in progress' because commit ran
while the result set was still pending.

The fix uses cursor.description to decide whether a statement produced a
result set, builds the DataFrame positionally from the cursor columns (so
duplicate column names survive), commits after consuming RETURNING rows, and
keeps the rows_affected contract for statements without a result set.

Adds an opt-in read_only=False parameter.  read_only=True opens the existing
file through a percent-encoded mode=ro URI, sets PRAGMA query_only and
installs a SQLite authorizer that refuses writes, ATTACH/DETACH, DDL and
write-capable PRAGMAs; a missing database is reported instead of created.
Default behaviour is unchanged.

Tests: real temporary SQLite databases, no mocks (tests/test_sqlite_runner_maintenance.py).
